subject: MedSupply: DPA redlines and SCCs — cross-border delegation/options
messages:

Cc: Jake Mullins <jake.mullins@medsupply.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on DPA / SCCs and transfer addendum

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal dug through your standard DPA and we have a short list of clarification requests before procurement can sign the MSA + Order Form:

1) SCCs approach — your DPA references SCCs but doesn't indicate whether Redwood intends to adopt the EU 2021 SCCs as-is or via an EU Addendum. We need the exact language we can attach to our side.
2) Roles & delegation — our data protection team wants explicit confirmation Redwood is a processor; will any subprocessors act as sub-processors located outside the EEA? Please attach the current subprocessor list and expected timeline for changes.
3) Transfer impact addendum — given we process EU patient data, can you confirm remediation steps if UK/EU authorities request additional safeguards?
4) KMS/key access — who holds the keys in practice if we opt for customer-managed keys?

I've attached MedSupply_DPA_Questions.pdf with inline comments. Our target is to finalize commercial terms and the DPA by 2027-06-14 to hit procurement windows.

Can someone from legal at Redwood loop in? Prefer a short call tomorrow afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Susan Park
VP Legal, MedSupply Inc.

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA / SCCs and transfer addendum — legal review notes

Tessa / Ben / Susan —

Thanks for the prompt. I reviewed RW_DPA_Redline_v1.docx and MedSupply_DPA_Questions.pdf. High-level summary and proposed route:

1) SCCs insertion: propose we adopt the EU 2021 SCCs via a short addendum clause in the DPA ("Attachment A - SCCs"). We'll provide the exact SCC text and a prefilled EU Addendum for signature. This avoids bespoke language and aligns with procurement expectations.

2) Roles & delegation: Redwood remains a processor. For clarity we will insert explicit controller/processor/processor-subprocessor table in Section 2 and include a delegation statement: Redwood may engage subprocessors (listed in manifest). Any subprocessor located outside the EEA will be covered by the SCCs and an internal review.

3) Subprocessor manifest: attached (subprocessor_manifest.csv) — current hosting, logging, monitoring vendors flagged. We recommend a standard "prior notice + 14-day objection" cadence for new subprocessors in the Order Form.

4) Transfer impact addendum: propose a short "Transfer Risk Mitigation" addendum: (a) specific technical measures (encryption in transit/rest, KV caching controls), (b) Fallback routing — where customer requests EU-only residency we'll include an Order Form flag to pin region and higher-tier SLA/cost. For cross-border remediation requests from regulators, Redwood will: triage, propose mitigations, and escalate to a named legal contact.

5) KMS / keys: we support customer-held keys via KMIP-compatible providers. Operationally: Redwood will not hold plaintext keys; we'll provide the integration spec. If MedSupply requires HSM-backed separation, that is doable under Dedicated/Private deployment and will carry a deployment/config fee (TBD).

Open items for MedSupply:
- Do you want Redwood to commit to EU-only processing in the Order Form or accept SCCs + fallback routing?
- Any special subprocessors to pre-block?

I attached a marked-up DPA (redwood_dpa_redline.docx) and the manifest. If the customer favors EU-only residency, we should surface cost/ops impact (dedicated capacity or private deployment). If SCCs route is acceptable, we can push a simple addendum and share countersign language by Friday 2027-06-11.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_dpa_redline.docx; subprocessor_manifest.csv

Karthik / Tessa —

Thanks for the clear options. Our privacy team reviewed and would prefer the SCCs addendum approach (keeps execution timeline shortest). A few quick replies:

- SCCs addendum: please share the prefilled SCC attachment and we'll loop legal to sign.
- Subprocessors: we reviewed the manifest; a couple of providers (listed in the PDF) need follow-up, but no immediate blocks. The 14-day objection cadence works for us.
- KMS: we'd like to proceed with customer-managed keys; please send the integration spec and any operational runbook.
- EU-only residency: not required for this deal provided SCCs + the Transfer Risk Mitigation addendum are in place.

Can Redwood produce a short procurement playbook (1-page) summarizing: DPA + SCCs addendum, subprocessor notice cadence, KMS integration steps, and expected timeline to signature? Our procurement deadline is EOD 2027-06-14. If you can get the prefilled SCCs and a one-page playbook over by 2027-06-10, we should be able to route and sign.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Susan Park
VP Legal, MedSupply Inc.
